paper.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: G-Memory, a three-tier (insight/query/interaction) agentic memory that evolves from collaborative trajectories, is a plug-and-play module that improves MAS success/accuracy (up to 20.89% embodied, 10.12% QA) without modifying the host frameworks.

signatures.operation: embedding top-k over query graph -> 1-hop expansion -> upward projection to insights, downward LLM-sparsified core trajectories -> role-conditioned projection Phi into each agent memory

signatures.later_use: every subsequent query in the same benchmark stream

signatures.failure_boundary: more hops / larger k add noise; ChatDev-M/MacNet-M/Voyager/MemoryBank sometimes degrade

gap.author_gap: MAS memory is overly simplistic (inside-trial or final-artifact only) and lacks cross-trial and agent-specific customization; single-agent memories do not carry over to MAS because trajectories are far longer.
gap.checked_gap: Partly corroborated inside the paper: adapted single-agent memories and MAS-native memories frequently fail to help or lower accuracy (E007). The token-length premise rests on a figure not readable in text. The gap is a real, non-weight object (agent memory), but the claimed bottleneck (flat memory vs hierarchical memory) is not tested against a matched flat insight+trajectory store.

matches.reason: Operation is: express a new query as retrieved insights and trajectories injected as context so a frozen MAS solves it without parameter updates. That is the card operation, but the card family is about trained conditioning channels; fit is partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest main card chosen by executed operation (retrieval-conditioned inference without weight updates); no sub card fits cleanly.

matches.reason: Store is reshaped into a three-tier graph with promotion/linking (query->insight support sets) and retrieval by traversal; claim rests on organization and traversal design (H04).
Insight nodes are LLM lessons from contrasting failed and successful trajectories (prompt in Appendix C), but the lesson layer is one tier of a larger index.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Both retrieve stored precedent and inject as context without weight updates; domain card adds store structure (tiers, graph, traversal) and write path that the RS card does not specify.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS card expects structural holdout and contamination audit; domain card adds selective retrieval, write gating, store-removal certification. Paper meets selective retrieval, partly store-removal, not write gating or holdout.

G.reason: Specific non-weight object (MAS memory) with a stated bottleneck and a lineage covering single-agent, MAS-native and automated-MAS neighbors; baseline degradation (E007) partly corroborates the gap. Not 4: ExpeL/A-Mem/Mem0 not run, hierarchy-vs-flat residual untested.

M.reason: Mechanism is reconstructable end to end (retrieve, traverse, sparsify, project per role, write insight/query/interaction levels) and predicts that role-specific delivery matters in PDDL; differentiation from the flat Generative baseline is argued but not isolated.

X.reason: Retrieval and write steps are explicit with equations and prompts, but retention governance is thin: all queries written incl. failed, consolidation prompt without trigger, no versioning/rollback/staleness handling, ordering and initial state unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmark metrics (success rate, progress rate, EM) with environment/label verification; but baselines are author-adapted, the AutoGen host has a reference-standard agent, and multi-trial evaluation protocol is not defined.

E.causality.reason: No-memory control in every setting and a two-component ablation exist; missing: flat-store/long-context equal-budget baseline, query-graph vs embedding-only retrieval, role projection and sparsifier ablations, and any improver-level comparison.

E.holdout.reason: Memory is built on the same queries that are scored, status feedback is label-derived, hop/k are tuned on reported results, no order control or contamination check; only breadth over 5 benchmarks and 3 backbones partially offsets.

E.statistics.reason: Negative baseline deltas are reported and the direction is consistent over 9 configurations, but no repeats, seeds, intervals or sample sizes (percent values suggest roughly 100-134 items per benchmark, our inference), so 1-2 item differences are unexplained.

E.cost.reason: Token-vs-performance figures and a stated modest increase; construction-time LLM calls (relevancy rating, sparsifier, insight writing) not clearly counted and no dollar or latency figures.

rationale: Plausible hierarchical memory plug-in with consistent in-stream gains over no-memory, but writes are ungated, evaluation shares queries with memory construction, and there is no variance or flat-store control; mid score driven by M/G, capped by E.holdout/statistics.
